This week covers **non-parametric tests** (Wilcoxon), **proportion tests** (Fisher / chi-square) for categorical data, and the **power of a test**. Use the language toggle above to switch between R and Python.

<h3>Quiz 1: Non-Parametric Tests <span id="quiz-done-w8_q_nonparam" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> When should you use a Wilcoxon test instead of a t-test?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np1" id="np1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="np1a">When the data is not normally distributed</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np1" id="np1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="np1b">When you have more than 1000 data points</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np1" id="np1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="np1c">When comparing more than 2 groups</label></div>
    <div id="np1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> The Wilcoxon test operates on the...</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np2" id="np2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="np2a">Raw values, exactly like the t-test</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np2" id="np2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="np2b">Ranks of the values, not the raw values themselves</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np2" id="np2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="np2c">Squared differences between values</label></div>
    <div id="np2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> In the plenum's by-hand computation, the U statistic (<code>U = R1 - n1(n1+1)/2</code>) is derived from...</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np3" id="np3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="np3a">The sum of ranks (R1) of one group, corrected for the group's own size</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np3" id="np3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="np3b">The mean of the raw values</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="np3" id="np3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="np3c">The standard deviation of the combined sample</label></div>
    <div id="np3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkNonparamQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="nonparam-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 2: Proportion Tests <span id="quiz-done-w8_q_proportion" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What kind of question are proportion tests (Fisher / chi-square) designed to answer?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt1" id="pt1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt1a">Whether the means of two continuous variables differ</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt1" id="pt1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt1b">Whether there is a significant relationship between two categorical variables</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt1" id="pt1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt1c">Whether a dataset follows a normal distribution</label></div>
    <div id="pt1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> An odds-ratio (OR) of exactly 1 in a 2×2 contingency table means...</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt2" id="pt2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt2a">There is no association between the two categorical variables</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt2" id="pt2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt2b">There is a perfect positive association</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt2" id="pt2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt2c">The test cannot be run</label></div>
    <div id="pt2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> The chi-square test statistic compares which two things?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt3" id="pt3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt3a">The observed counts in the contingency table vs. the counts expected if there were no relationship</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt3" id="pt3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt3b">Two means</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt3" id="pt3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt3c">Two standard deviations</label></div>
    <div id="pt3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkProportionQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="proportion-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 3: Power of a Test <span id="quiz-done-w8_q_power" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> In the biomarker diagnostic example, what does β (the Type II error rate) represent?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw1" id="pw1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw1a">The false-positive rate — diagnosing a healthy patient as sick</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw1" id="pw1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw1b">The false-negative rate — failing to detect the condition in a patient who actually has it</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw1" id="pw1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw1c">The proportion of patients tested</label></div>
    <div id="pw1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> The power of a test is defined as...</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw2" id="pw2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw2a">α, the significance level</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw2" id="pw2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw2b">1 − β, the probability of correctly detecting a real effect</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw2" id="pw2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw2c">The sample mean</label></div>
    <div id="pw2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Which of the following would <strong>increase</strong> the power of the diagnostic test in the example?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw3" id="pw3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw3a">Taking fewer measurements per patient (smaller n)</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw3" id="pw3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw3b">Taking more measurements per patient (larger n), which shrinks the standard error</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pw3" id="pw3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pw3c">Ignoring the significance level entirely</label></div>
    <div id="pw3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkPowerQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="power-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 4: False Positives, False Negatives &amp; FDR (Plenum) <span id="quiz-done-w8_q_errors" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> When H0 is actually true, what should the distribution of p-values look like across many repeated tests?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd1" id="fd1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd1a">Uniformly distributed between 0 and 1</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd1" id="fd1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd1b">Always exactly 0.05</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd1" id="fd1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd1c">Concentrated near 0</label></div>
    <div id="fd1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> In the plenum's gene expression simulation (900 genes with no real difference, 100 genes with a real difference), what does the False Discovery Rate (FDR) measure?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd2" id="fd2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd2a">The proportion of all 1000 genes that are truly different</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd2" id="fd2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd2b">The proportion of genes called "significant" (test-positive) that are actually false positives</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd2" id="fd2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd2c">The total number of genes tested</label></div>
    <div id="fd2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Why does the FPR (false-positive rate) stop equaling α when the data is not normally distributed and you still use a t-test?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd3" id="fd3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd3a">Because the t-test's theoretical guarantees rely on the normality assumption, which is violated</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd3" id="fd3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd3b">Because R computes p-values incorrectly for non-normal data</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fd3" id="fd3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="fd3c">α always equals the FPR no matter what</label></div>
    <div id="fd3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkErrorsQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="errors-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>
